In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for a stiff polytropically supported neutron star and high mass ratios, a black hole-neutron star binary system is dynamically unstable and decays.

for a sufficiently large initial mass ratio, the system becomes unstable due to tidal forces, and the neutron star is not tidally disrupted, but instead forms a stable accretion toroidal structure around the black hole.
for a sufficiently high mass ratio the system will be unstable to hydrodynamic instabilities, and will decay within a few dynamical timescales.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the evolution of tidally locked neutron star-black hole binaries depends on the initial separation, mass ratio, and the equation of state for the neutron star, and the evolution of the system is dominated by hydrodynamical and tidal forces.
for a stiff polytrope and a black hole of a few solar masses, we find that the neutron star is not disrupted by tidal forces, but that the binary may still coalesce due to hydrodynamics.
for a mass ratio q = 1, the system becomes unstable and the neutron star is disrupted on a dynamical time scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of gravitational radiation, the neutron star can remain bound to the black hole, and a significant amount of matter can survive the encounter.
, for the stiff polytroper considered in the present paper, the coalescence process is dominated by the tidal interaction between the neutron star and the black hole.
